categories.name: Calamari
categories.description: Calamari have a strong muscled mantle which gradually tapers to the fins, then sharply to the tail. The fins are wide and triangular. The skin is light and smooth with a brownish-pink to red with a bluish purple dorsal stripe. The cartilage that connects the mantle to the funnel is shaped like an inverted ‘T’. Calamari have a subtle taste and are firm yet tender. Squid is popularly served as deep fried rings.

categories.name: Gummy Shark
categories.metaTitle: Gummy Shark - I'm Hooked Fishing Charters
categories.description: Gummy sharks are a relatively small slender-bodied species with a short head. They are grey above and white below, with white spots on the back and upper sides. The second dorsal fin is nearly as large as the first dorsal fin. The mouth is short and angular with numerous rows of blunt, flattened teeth. Gummy sharks are highly targeted fish, often marketed as "flake" in southern Australia. Their boneless fillets have made them particularly popular within the 'fish and chips' industry.

categories.name: Kingfish
categories.description: The kingfish is a medium-sized fish ranging in weight from 5 to 14 kg, but can also exceed 40 kg in some cases. Its body is covered with small, almost invisible, loosely attached scales. The first dorsal fin is entirely colourless and normally folded back into a body groove, as are the pelvic fins. Its colour is olive on the back, morphing to silver with a rosy radiancy on the sides, fading to white on the belly. Smaller kingfish that are under 5 kg show yellow-brown spots on the sides. Its cutting-edged teeth are large and closely spaced and flattened from side to side.

categories.name: Snapper
categories.description: The Snapper found in Australia, also called silver seabream, is a species of porgie found in coastal waters of Australia and New Zealand amongst other places. Although it is almost universally known in Australia and New Zealand as snapper, it does not belong to the snapper family (Lutjanidae). It is a highly sought after edible fish, with a sweet sea taste and a firm texture.

categories.name: Tuna
categories.description: Tuna are a saltwater ocean fish that belong to the Thunnini tribe, a subgrouping of the mackerel family. They comprise 15 species, the sizes of which vary greatly, ranging from the bullet tuna (max length: 50 cm, weight: 1.8 kg) up to the Atlantic bluefin tuna (max length: 4.6 m, weight: 684 kg). They average 2 m in length and are believed to live up to 50 years. Tuna can maintain a body temperature higher than that of the surrounding water. They are an active and agile predator with a sleek, streamlined shape and are among the fastest swimming fish. The yellowfin tuna is capable of speeds of up to 75 km/h. Found in warm seas, the tuna is commercially fished extensively for food and is popular as a bluewater game fish. As a result of overfishing, some tuna species, such as the southern bluefin tuna, are threatened with extinction.

categories.name: Whiting
categories.description: Whiting, commonly known as the smelt-whitings, or sillaginids, sand borers and sand-smelts, are a family of coastal marine fish in the order Perciformes. Whiting inhabit a wide region which covers much of the Indo-Pacific. This includes an area from the west coast of Africa to Japan and south to Australia. The family comprises only five genera and around 35 species. They are elongated, slightly compressed fish, often light brown to silver in colour, with a variety of markings and patterns on their upper bodies. The Sillaginidae are not related to a number of fishes commonly called 'whiting' in the Northern Hemisphere, including the fish originally called whiting, Merlangius merlangus.
